assumptions.objective: Current domestic provincial tax receipts in koku per turn; not GDP, total campaign income or treasury profit.
assumptions.ownership: The selected provinces are jointly owned; food and unique-building limits are faction-wide.
assumptions.town_wealth: Explicit, fixed scenario input. Default zero isolates income from chosen buildings; it is not a historical start state.
assumptions.tax_and_order: Common base tax rate 30%, administration multiplier 1, normal-tax unrest -4, minimum public order 0 unless overridden. No governors, agents, garrisons, honour or difficulty bonuses.
assumptions.religion: Each clan's native faith, 100% local adherence. No conversion timeline or religious unrest at this snapshot.
assumptions.research_and_resources: All imported arts researched, all prerequisite construction resources accessible; no construction budget or sequencing. Arts food is counted once per faction.
assumptions.eligibility: Native religious chains, Otomo-specific Christian branch, location-specific specialty and port plots, one chain per town slot, castle-level slot capacity, one new legendary town building of each chain per faction, one new Nanban chain. No captured unique duplicates; Jesuit Colleges are not legendary.
assumptions.growth: Building, arts and shared-food growth components are reported, not valued in the current-income objective. Tax-induced growth penalties and future wealth dynamics are not simulated. Tied layouts can have different growth.
assumptions.excluded_income_and_costs: Trade/export/tribute income, the common clan stipend, military/agent expenses, first-construction race rewards and campaign bonuses excluded. Uesugi's trade trait therefore has no contribution. One-off Portuguese land sale excluded. Military-only buildings cannot improve this objective and are omitted.
assumptions.validation_limit: Optimality applies to this public-reference static model, not an exhaustive or installed-build-verified campaign simulation. Province prose yields do not override structured building effects.
